image_prompt.text: Rooftop plant rooms, water towers and street-level columns scattered through the city, so a player being chased can break line of sight while still moving
Open rooftop edges and unguarded drops to the street below, so a missed jump costs you
Alleys, narrow ledges and single skybridges between blocks that funnel players onto the same crossing
Ordinary city residents going about their day — pedestrians on the sidewalks, shopkeepers in doorways, small crowds at the intersections
A dense city block grid of continuous built-up streets rather than scattered individual buildings

layout_placement.text: The sidewalks, doorways and intersections the city's non-hostile residents occupy

notes: Preset Parkour Traversal taken whole, shape included; nothing in the prompt contradicted any of its three options.
Shape call was close between traversal-city and world-open, and it turns entirely on what 'cool movement' means. Read as parkour geometry, so the city is built to be crossed over.

traversal-city carries P2 and is not on the shape-route override list, so the route is P2. If 'cool movement' turns out to mean movement abilities rather than rooftop traversal, world-open at P0 is the shape and the build stays on the proven route. Recorded rather than downgraded silently.
'powers' and 'cool movement' are gameplay, so they sit in mechanics; only their spatial consequence, a city sized and surfaced to be moved through, is in the map.
No terminating place emitted. An open powers-and-parkour city is a place you roam rather than a run that ends, so no winner-zone or exit was inferred.
settlement-density restates the city the chosen shape already implies. Kept because the prompt named the city outright and there is no rule for deduping a shape against an option.

'cool movement' as the character controller itself — dashing, wall-running, double jumps

skill_gap.name: no option for movement affordances
skill_gap.why: The spatial half of 'cool movement' — wall-run surfaces, gaps sized to a dash, grapple or swing points — has no row in Action's table, the universal six, or options.md. Its only home is the shape, which is exclusive and chosen once, so the request cannot be expressed as a feature and disappears if any other shape wins. That in turn forces the P2 that traversal-city carries, with no sanctioned way to keep the movement and stay on the proven route.

notes_for_us: Action's Typical shapes line gives bare IDs; only the two shapes it rewords have full rows. Emitting shape.type and shape.name for traversal-city forced loading shapes.md even though a typical shape fitted, which the brief treats as the miss case.

Step 4's 'prefer P0 and P6' collides with shape choice: traversal-city carries P2 and is not on the route-override list, so honouring the prompt's city-parkour reading forces an undeliverable route and the only escape is picking a different shape.
layout-intake mandates a theme open question whenever theme is silent, while genre-choice step 5 caps questions at four. This prompt had five real holes, so the two rules cannot both be obeyed.
No rule covers deduping a shape against an option expressing the same thing — traversal-city and settlement-density both ship the city, and only options dedupe by ID.
'in a city' is a setting the theme table would read straight off as Modern Urban, but layout-intake says never guess theme. Whether a named setting counts as a stated theme is undefined.
